+2422

Zero high-jump squares does not mean you cannot hop over a low obstacle. The grid measures large clearances. Safe jumps within your limits need no roll; a risky landing can call for Agility. Jumping does not grant extra movement or passage through a barrier.

Falling deals 3 physical damage per complete 2 squares fallen. Round the distance down to complete pairs before multiplying; normal physical resistance applies. A fall of 5 squares deals 6 damage before resistance. A fall under 2 squares has no automatic falling damage. Exceptional surfaces and landing circumstances are DA rulings.

Talk, bargain and persuade

Speak for your character, summarize what they say, or use a mixture of both. Explain what you want and why the other person might agree. The DA portrays their interests, knowledge and limits. A roll resolves uncertainty; it does not erase their motives.

Use the attribute printed on a social ability. Without one, the DA calls for an attribute appropriate to the approach. Guile might carry a deceptive bargain; Knowledge might establish a technical argument; Reason might find the important contradiction. A useful fact or appropriate gesture can make a roll unnecessary.

A scar's intimidation Boon or persuasion Bane applies when the scar actually influences the interaction. The DA decides that circumstance, just as they decide whether a wound affects a physical activity. Personality and allegiance remain choices, not penalties assigned by a condition table.

Magic in your hands

Magic is learned through abilities and disciplines. There are no spell slots or mana pools. A spell uses the same action, attribute and outcome structure as another ability, with its printed requirements and costs. An attack spell still produces its Weak result on a Weak roll; it does not simply fizzle.

You choose a card before rolling. A line, rectangle or placed area must use its printed dimensions and range. Connected placed squares share edges. Decide targets and any damage-type choice before rolling. An illustration or evocative description does not silently make the area larger or add a condition.

Defensive interference and disruption are supplied by abilities. There is no universal spell-cancellation roll. Casting beside an enemy can provoke an opportunity attack; resolve it before continuing the spell if still capable.

Beast forms keep your own HP, attributes and wounds. They are not replaceable HP pools. Use the form's printed actions and equipment restrictions. A form does not import an entire monster entry or grant spellcasting if its rules forbid it.

Moser's law of conservation of Life energy

Healing magic transfers life energy; it does not create it freely. A Novice healing spell costs its caster 1 HP, an Adept spell 3 HP, and a Master spell 7 HP. Pay the full cost before rolling. This cost bypasses all resistance and must leave the caster above 0 HP. You cannot begin a healing spell by sacrificing your last HP. The cost applies regardless of the tradition used to describe the spell.

Healing requires a free hand. Restore the outcome's printed fixed HP, reduce it by the recipient's Life resistance, and restore at least 1 if HP is missing. Never exceed maximum HP. Healing does not erase wounds or reverse Last Words. Potions have their own fixed value and inventory procedure, without a spell outcome roll or caster cost.

> Example — energy has a price. A Novice healer at 5 HP pays 1 and falls to 4, > then rolls the spell. If its outcome restores 4 HP to a companion with Life > resistance 2, the companion regains 2. The caster cannot use the same spell at > 1 HP, because paying first would leave them at 0.

A healing spell can attack a creature whose profile says healing harms it. Use the spell's attack attribute, range and cost. Its HP result becomes Life damage; beneficial recovery riders do not help that target. This follows the ordinary player-roll procedure, with no extra opposed save.

Make, identify and derive

A crafting card grants the capability to work; a recipe describes the specific thing you can make. Recipes specify permission, tools, materials, time and output. Choose the recipes granted when learning your crafting ability. Ordinary Recipe Study offers additional eligible recipes through DP. Other recipes can be found or derived; they are not automatically on sale for coins.

Acquire the actual ingredients. Foraged materials need not be carried indefinitely; carried bundles use their printed Bulk and inventory die. Complete the recipe's full time, roll the crafting card's attribute, and increase one existing product supply by 1/2/3 inventory steps as the recipe allows. Starting from out, the first step is d4. Never exceed the recipe's cap. Check carried material supply after use.

Derivation is reverse engineering, not the same as identification. Identification cards reveal what their outcomes say; an item may require that understanding before use. A magical sword may work at once, while a tome may remain unusable until understood. A derivation card specifies its target and work interval. Exceptional objects can require years of accumulated work. No group crafting or group derivation shortens it.

Rest and development

The DA determines whether a place is safe enough to spend saved DP. Level awards are milestones, not payment for each defeated creature. Keep a record of purchases, prerequisites, recipes and scars so your development remains clear.

A wound may require repeated daily treatment even after you are ready to adventure. An inn, a friendly workshop, a healer's garden or a camp among allies can become part of the story. Rest restores what its rule says it restores. It does not refund Grit, remove a permanent scar, or refill a bottle whose inventory die is out.

A familiar greeting can open a door that gold cannot. An inscription can preserve an enemy's warning long after the enemy is dust. Languages tell you whom your hero can understand and which voices shaped their life. They do not determine ancestry, allegiance or character.

Choose your languages

Begin with Common and one other ordinary language learned in the community that raised you. Common is the campaign's shared trade language; the DA may give it a local name. Choose your other language with the DA from the list below or the campaign's equivalent. Any ancestry may know any language. Culture suggests where you learned it, rather than imposing a compulsory choice.

Record the language's actual name, not just “regional” or “community language.” If Common was your only home language, choose another ordinary language learned through neighbors, work or travel. This starting choice is separate from your culture's discipline and ability pair and costs no DP.

Apply explicit extra grants afterward. A Foot in Two Worlds grants two additional ordinary spoken languages. Choose two distinct languages you do not already know; it does not grant another culture's abilities. A signed language is an ordinary language when the campaign uses it, but a grant restricted to spoken languages does not include it.

Unless a grant says otherwise, knowing a language includes speaking, understanding, and reading and writing its usual script, if it has one. A grant that specifically says spoken, understands or cannot speak keeps that restriction. Record such limits beside the language. Speaking a language does not require a separate skill rating, and attributes grant no automatic extra languages.

Ordinary languages

These are starting options, not a required history of the world. Their names describe familiar traditions; anyone raised among their speakers may learn them. Each row is one language unless it explicitly asks you to name a particular one.

LanguageWhere you might learn or encounter it

DwarvenDeep halls, quarry towns and craft communities; records of lineage, work and agreements.

Uncommon and ancient languages

These languages are not included in an unrestricted ordinary language grant. Choose one only when a grant explicitly allows it or the DA makes it an ordinary option for the campaign before character creation. Their availability reflects the setting, not a higher numerical bonus.

A sacred text may be written in Common, Dwarven or any other language. “Sacred,” “scholarly” and “courtly” describe use, not automatic additional languages. Beasts' calls, a spirit's images and a construct's signal lights are forms of communication, not languages you gain by choosing a row in these tables.

Use languages at the table

When you share a language and can hear, see or read it as required, ordinary communication needs no roll. State what you say or ask. A conversation can still involve uncertainty about persuasion, deception or evidence; use the normal attribute or the ability you declared. Knowing the words does not make the listener agree, reveal secrets or recognize your authority.

A language barrier is not simply extra Banes on a roll. Without a shared means of communication, you cannot deliver a precise argument merely by rolling well. Pointing, drawing or demonstrating can convey something simple: “danger there,” “follow me,” or an offered trade. Agree on what is actually understood. An interpreter, a translation, or an applicable ability can make a more complicated exchange possible. A card that explicitly requires a shared language still requires one; an interpreter does not silently change its target requirement.

Reading a clear message in a language you can read needs no roll. Damaged text, an unfamiliar technical subject or a cipher may present a separate problem. Sharing an alphabet does not grant another language, and a cipher is not an extra language choice. Ask the DA what evidence or expertise could make progress possible.

Translate the Fragment supplies a way to interpret unfamiliar written text. Use its printed time, progress and outcomes. Completing a translation does not teach you the whole language. A copied voice or disguise likewise supplies no vocabulary or memories unless its ability explicitly says so.

Learn another language

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.b2ef1858c60e2bb9]{Another Tongue} costs 1 DP and grants one additional ordinary language, including its usual script if it has one. It requires no discipline and may be purchased once, during level-0 creation or later. Record the language you choose. This is a specific card grant, not a repeatable price for buying every language or permission to learn a secret language.

Keep learning grounded

Record new languages when an explicit trait, ability or agreed campaign grant provides them. Time with a teacher, a community or useful texts explains that learning; it does not create an unstated free advancement or a new universal DP price. Agree on the route before spending time or DP. Translation and ordinary practice remain useful even when they do not grant permanent fluency.

> At the gate. An elf raised in a dwarven mining town chooses Common and > Dwarven. She reads the quarry's warning without a roll. Its damaged diagram > still needs investigation. Her human companion's extra spoken Goblin lets him > question a salvager, but does not let him read the salvager's written ledger.

You can catch your breath after a battle. You cannot always leave the battle behind. HP measures your immediate capacity to keep going. Grit gives you a limited reserve when you fall. Wounds record the lasting cost, even when their active penalties have been treated.

Subtract damage from current HP. Healing restores its printed amount, after any Life resistance, up to maximum HP. When the immediate danger has passed and you can safely take a breath, restore HP to full. The DA determines whether that pause is safe. A breath does not erase a wound or replenish spent Grit.

Deal with immediate conditions as the fiction permits. Companions can put out an ordinary fire when no danger prevents them from doing so. Poison, persistent injuries and other unresolved conditions do not all disappear because combat ended. Use each condition's removal rule. Resolve a Dying character's situation before leaving turn timing.

You can catch your breath after a battle. You cannot always leave the battle behind. HP measures your immediate capacity to keep going. Grit gives you a limited reserve when you fall. Wounds record the lasting cost, even when their active penalties have been treated.

HP, healing and a safe breath

Subtract damage from current HP. Healing restores its printed amount, after any Life resistance, up to maximum HP. When the immediate danger has passed and you can safely take a breath, restore HP to full. The DA determines whether that pause is safe. A breath does not erase a wound or replenish spent Grit.

Deal with immediate conditions as the fiction permits. Companions can put out an ordinary fire when no danger prevents them from doing so. Poison, persistent injuries and other unresolved conditions do not all disappear because combat ended. Use each condition's removal rule. Resolve a Dying character's situation before leaving turn timing.

When you fall

Player characters enter Dying at 0 HP. Each entry causes a new wound. A creature or ordinary NPC normally dies at 0 HP; player-character survival procedures are not a second HP pool for every opponent.

Roll the new wound immediately. Roll three d6, plus one extra die for each prior wound, to a maximum of five dice total. Retain the highest three, sort them from lowest to highest, and read them as a three-digit number. Add the new scar to your wound count after determining this roll.

> Example — a second scar. You already have one wound, so roll four dice for > the next one. On 2, 4, 4, 6, keep 4, 4, 6: result 446. Read 446 on the appropriate > wound table. It is not a total of fourteen. Even after treatment, your earlier scar > still adds its die to this roll.

Choose the table for the damage type that dealt the most damage after resistance. You choose on a tie. Physical includes sonic and force. Fire, Cold and Lightning use Elemental wounds, but keep separate resistances. Mental, Radiant and Life/Necrotic have their own tables.

> Fully resisted components. If an event dealt only its minimum > 1 total damage because all components were reduced to zero, choose a wound table > from the event's original damage types. The player chooses which one applies.

If the listed body part is absent or the injury cannot apply, move to the next listed result until one does, such as 116 to 122. Do not reroll for a more convenient injury. The tables end at 666.

Your Dying turn

At the start of your turn while Dying, choose one Grit or a death roll. This choice stands for the turn; you cannot see the roll and then decide to spend Grit.

Spend one Grit to regain full HP. You retain the wound you just suffered. Otherwise, roll Fortitude and apply the death-roll result.

Death-roll resultEffect
WeakGain 1 death mark.
StandardNo change.
StrongStabilize at 0 HP and clear death marks.
Retained natural 111Gain 2 death marks instead of the ordinary Weak result.
Retained natural 666Restore 1 HP and clear death marks.

At three death marks, enter Last Words. Damage while already Dying adds one mark per damaging event; it does not create another wound. Damage that returns a stabilized character to Dying creates a new wound and adds one death mark.

A companion can use the universal Stabilize Maneuver. Stabilization clears death marks and leaves you at 0 HP, unable to act. Healing above 0 clears death marks and ends HP-caused unconsciousness. It does not necessarily remove another condition that also prevents action.

Last Words

A wound result of 666, or reaching three death marks, begins Last Words. You can speak, but do nothing else. You die at the end of the second following turn. Use that time for a farewell, a warning, a promise or silence. It belongs to the player.

Ordinary healing, treatment, potions and Grit cannot reverse Last Words. Only an explicit exceptional ability could say otherwise. Another character's ability may react to hearing those words without changing the finality of your death.

Treating a wound

A wound states its immediate effect, any lasting penalty, its required treatment and Recovery Value, or RV. Immediate pushes and knockdowns happen once. Temporary conditions decay under the condition rules. Lasting wound penalties remain until their stated remedy.

Use the appropriate treatment card: Soft Tissue, Bone, Mental, Elemental, Radiant or Life. Each attempt takes the card's full time. A wound can receive only one treatment attempt per day, across all healers. Weak, Standard and Strong add 1, 2 and 3 recovery progress. Keep accumulated progress with the wound.

When progress meets or exceeds RV, remove exactly the effects its remedy says it removes. The scar and accumulated wound count remain. Treatment does not regrow a missing limb. An artificial replacement or exceptional ability specifies the function it restores. Rest works as a remedy only when the wound explicitly lists it.

> Example — two different problems. Physical wound 333 applies Bleeding 1 and > a lasting Bane. Bleeding resolves and decays, or can be reduced with an appropriate > Main Action. It does not restart each turn because the scar exists. Soft Tissue > treatment must accumulate RV 3 to remove the lasting Bane. The scar still counts > on every later wound roll.

A cosmetic wound can need no treatment. If treating a socially significant scar removes its intimidation Boon and persuasion Bane, remove both, as printed. The DA decides when broad physical or mental activity penalties apply.

Temporary and lasting conditions

Read the condition's source as well as its name. An ability, wound or other effect says how the condition begins and which remedy ends it. A rating, an asterisk and a wound's Recovery Value tell you different things.

What you recordWhat time doesHow it ends
Temporary numbered condition, such as Bleeding 3 or Blinded 2At the end of your turn, resolve its effect, then reduce its temporary rating by 1Reaching 0, or a remedy that applies to that condition
Starred condition, such as Blinded 1*The starred rating stays until its remedy appliesThe source's specified treatment, replacement or other remedy
Lasting wound penalty, such as a Bane or movement lossThe penalty stays until its printed remedy appliesComplete that wound's treatment or another remedy the wound lists
Maintained or binary state, such as Grappled or ProneFollow that state's own rulesRelease or escape the grapple; spend 2 movement to stand from Prone

Temporary means the numbered contribution decays automatically. A condition gained during your turn also decreases at that turn's end. The number may measure severity, duration, or both: Blinded 2 prevents sight until it clears, while Dazed can restrict fewer action categories as its rating falls.

Lasting means the effect stays until its remedy. An asterisk marks no automatic decay. It does not mean incurable: Blinded 1* can be treatable when its source says so. Some injuries cause permanent loss; those entries identify replacement or an exceptional remedy rather than ordinary treatment. Rest restores HP when safe; a lasting condition follows its own remedy.

Removing a lasting condition

1. Find its source. Read the ability or wound that applied it. For a wound, record its table and result, lasting effects, Treatment / remedy and RV. 2. Use the listed remedy. A treatment label identifies the required capability: Soft Tissue, Bone, Mental, Elemental, Radiant or Life. A replacement or special cure instead follows its own procedure. A dash in RV means there is no treatment progress track; read the remedy column. 3. Track recovery where an RV is printed. Use the matching treatment ability and its full time. One wound receives one attempt per day across all healers. Add 1, 2 or 3 progress for Weak, Standard or Strong and keep that progress. 4. Remove the effects the remedy names. Reaching RV completes that wound's treatment. The scar still counts toward future wound rolls. A replacement restores only the function its remedy specifies.

> Example: two kinds of blindness. Blinded 2 from a temporary effect clears > after two end-of-turn decay steps. Physical wound 366 instead causes Blinded 1* > and lists Soft Tissue treatment, RV 5. A Standard treatment adds 2 progress; a > Strong treatment on a later day adds 3. At 5, sight returns. The scar remains.

When temporary and lasting effects overlap

Record temporary and starred contributions separately. Add effective severity where the condition uses severity, but decay only the temporary part. For a duration-only condition, either positive contribution keeps the condition active. An ability that reduces temporary Dazed affects that temporary contribution; lasting treatment follows its source.

If an eye injury already causes Blinded 1* and dust adds temporary Blinded 2, clearing the dust leaves the wound's blindness in place. Treating the eye injury resolves its starred contribution; any remaining temporary blindness follows its own decay or remedy.

Dazed and Grappled determine your retained action categories at turn start. A change during the turn does not undo actions already spent or recalculate that turn's category selection. Grappled still prevents movement while the hold exists. Paralyzed, Asleep and Unconscious impose their immediate restrictions.

You can spend a Main Action to reduce Bleeding, Burning or Freezing on yourself or an adjacent creature by 1 with a plausible method. This is not a cure for every condition. Specialized cards may remove more or use a cheaper action.

> Example — resolve, then decay. Untreated Bleeding 3 deals 3 damage at turn end, > then becomes Bleeding 2. On later turns it deals 2 and then 1 before ending. > Reducing it with a Main Action before the first tick changes the sequence to 2, > then 1. Bleeding bypasses resistance; Burning and Freezing use matching resistance.

Asleep, Paralyzed, Unconscious and Petrified impose three defense Banes. Overlapping helpless states apply that penalty once. Dazed adds no defense Banes. Grappled gives attackers one Boon per rating of the actual target. When Dazed and Grappled overlap, use the greater action restriction, not their sum.

You plant an armored fist, roll the weight beneath you, and rise already moving.

Target / range / shape: Self while wearing armor.

Stand if Prone, then move up to 2 squares without provoking.

Equipment / acquisition: Worn armor.

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

Agreed condition rules, consolidated after the wound-table review (issue #1125). Use these timing and sensory rules throughout the current catalog.

Ratings, decay, and persistence

At the end of the affected character's turn, resolve a temporary numbered condition's effect, then reduce its rating by 1. At 0 it ends. A condition gained during that turn also decreases at that turn's end. Numbered instances add where meaningful; binary states do not. Normal Boon/Bane cancellation and caps apply.

The number can describe severity as well as duration (Dazed, Burning), or duration only (Blinded, Paralyzed). A higher duration-only rating does not strengthen the condition. Dazed 3 or greater grants no action categories.

An asterisk means no automatic decay: Blinded 1* is blindness that persists until its specified remedy. It does not mean every such injury is incurable. A wound states whether treatment, replacement, or another remedy removes it. Maintained Grappled does not decay. Binary conditions and lasting wound penalties use their own removal rules.

Spend a Main Action to reduce an appropriate condition on yourself or an adjacent creature by 1 without a roll: staunch Bleeding, extinguish Burning, or warm someone suffering Freezing with a plausible method. This is not a universal cure for every condition. Specialist abilities can remove more or use a cheaper action. A star prevents automatic decay, not a removal method explicitly allowed by its source. Record temporary and starred contributions separately, using the mixed-source tracking procedure below.

Example: untreated Bleeding 3 deals 3 damage, decreases to 2, then deals 2 and 1 on subsequent turns before ending. A Main Action reducing it before the first tick changes that sequence to 2, then 1. Burning and Freezing apply matching resistance to each tick, with the normal minimum 1 damage for a damaging event.

Temporary and lasting conditions

A temporary numbered contribution resolves and decays at the end of the affected creature's turn. A starred contribution has no automatic decay. A lasting wound penalty remains until its printed remedy. Maintained Grappled and binary Prone instead use their own release, escape or standing rules.

An asterisk means persistent, not necessarily incurable. To remove a lasting effect, find the ability or wound that caused it and follow its stated remedy. For a wound with a treatment label and Recovery Value (RV), use the matching treatment capability. One attempt per wound per day adds 1/2/3 progress; reaching RV removes the effects named by that remedy. A dash in RV means no treatment track. Replacement and exceptional remedies follow their own printed procedure. Scars remain after functional recovery.

For example, Physical wound 366 causes Blinded 1* and lists Soft Tissue treatment, RV 5. Standard treatment adds 2 progress, and Strong treatment on a later day adds 3; reaching 5 restores sight. Temporary Blinded 2 instead clears through two end-of-turn decay steps. A safe breath restores HP while a lasting condition continues to follow its remedy.

Asleep, Paralyzed, Unconscious, and Petrified apply three defense Banes; overlapping helpless states apply that penalty once. Dazed adds no defense Banes. Attacks against a Grappled creature gain one Boon per level of its Grappled rating, including attacks against grapplers, using normal Boon/Bane rules. When Dazed and Grappled coexist, use the greater action restriction, not their sum.

Grappling restricts the grappler by their own contribution as well as the target. Multiple grapplers' contributions add on the target. Each can freely release even at rating 3, ending their contribution. Once helpless capture is established and combat is over, resolve the scene through ordinary narration.

Example: Paralyzed 3 prevents actions and movement, falls to 2 at turn end, then to 1, then clears. Dazed 3 instead gradually returns action options as it decays. Blinded 2 is full blindness for two decay steps, not stronger blindness than 1.

Provisional prone combat rider for tests: none beyond movement until approved. Do not import automatic melee Boons or ranged Banes from another game's prone rule.

See @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.401d23f4b66980ee]{wounds} for lasting effects and @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.83082c8f9728466c]{foundations} for movement.

Action-category timing — latest agreement

Dazed and Grappled determine retained action categories at the start of the affected creature’s turn. Changes during the turn do not undo spent actions or recalculate that turn’s category selection. Temporary Dazed decays at turn end; maintained Grappled does not decay. Grappled’s movement restriction still applies while the hold exists. Paralyzed, Asleep and Unconscious retain their immediate restrictions; they are not action-category selection effects.

Mixed-source tracking: record temporary and starred contributions separately. Add effective severity where the condition uses severity; decay only the temporary part. For duration-only conditions, either positive contribution keeps the condition active, without multiplying its effect. Generic temporary reduction removes temporary rating only; permanent treatment follows its source.

Agreed foundation retained from the design conversation, not old ability text.

HP returns to full after a safe breath. Grit and wounds do not reset. Each entry into Dying causes a wound, including damage that returns a stabilized character to Dying. At the start of a Dying character’s turn, choose Grit or the death roll; that choice stands for the turn. Stabilization is a universal Maneuver. Ordinary healing can return a living character to activity but cannot remove their scar.

Wound roll: 3d6 plus one die per prior wound, capped at the approved working limit of five dice; retain the highest three, sort ascending, read as a three-digit result. Only 666 reaches the 600 band. It gives Last Words: two rounds of speech only, then final death. Exceptional reversal abilities are not supplied casually here.

Physical, Elemental, Mental, Radiant and Life/Necrotic wound tables are now consolidated in the @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.401d23f4b66980ee]{fresh wound reference}, copied from the approved working tables without changing their 280 results. Historical playtest files remain unchanged. @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.b8dbac21301a8aa3]{Conditions} supplies the full condition reference.

Treatments require the correct capability. Each wound has a recovery value and states exactly which penalties completing treatment relieves. Weak/Standard/Strong adds 1/2/3 recovery, at most one treatment per wound per day across all healers. Scars and accumulated wound count remain. Lost parts require an explicit replacement or exceptional remedy; generic treatment does not regrow them.

Fresh treatment cards cover Soft Tissue, Bone, Mental, Elemental, Radiant and Life injury. The treatment label map below identifies the matching cards; similar-sounding abilities are not automatically interchangeable.

Death and Grit procedure

At the start of a Dying turn, spend one Grit to regain full HP or make a Fortitude roll. Weak adds one death mark; Standard changes nothing; Strong stabilizes at 0 and clears marks. Fumble adds two marks; Critical restores 1 HP and clears marks. Three marks cause Last Words. Damage while already Dying adds one mark per event, not another wound. Damage while stabilized adds the new wound and one mark.

Healing above 0 clears death marks. Stabilization clears marks but leaves you at 0 and unable to act. Resolve Dying before ending combat; a breath does not erase a pending death. Last Words ends in death at the end of the second following turn.

This procedure is transcribed from the agreed survival reference, not designed from an old card. Ordinary potion/spell healing cannot reverse Last Words.

Each attempt takes the card’s hour, once per wound per day across all healers. Physical prostheses follow their recipe and actual remedy; no treatment regrows a limb or refunds the accumulated wound count.

An ability is a practiced technique, a spell, a talent or a reliable piece of expertise. Its first lines describe what your hero does. Its rules tell you how that moment changes the game. Declare the ability before rolling and use its printed attribute.

The numbered diamond is the minimum level: 1 Novice, 3 Adept, or 7 Master. Novice purchases are allowed in level-0 creation. Discipline abilities normally cost 2, 4 or 8 DP. Paid abilities without discipline requirements print their own prices: 1 or 2 DP at Novice, 3 DP at Adept, and 6 or 8 DP at Master. Every listed discipline rank must be owned before learning. No earlier card is required merely because its name or theme resembles a later one. The symbols beside a card name identify its disciplines; each discipline entry shows its symbol. Full requirements are also written out, so you never have to identify a symbol alone.

Universal actions are available to everyone. Their diamond reads U and they cost no DP, but they do not give you free equipment. The shared catalog follows by tier, alphabetically within each tier. Your class's signature choices are printed with that class. Each tier opens with a quick selection table. The tiered index at the back includes shared and class signature abilities, with requirements and page references.

An ability is a practiced technique, a spell, a talent or a reliable piece of expertise. Its first lines describe what your hero does. Its rules tell you how that moment changes the game. Declare the ability before rolling and use its printed attribute.

The numbered diamond is the minimum level: 1 Novice, 3 Adept, or 7 Master. Novice purchases are allowed in level-0 creation. Discipline abilities normally cost 2, 4 or 8 DP. Paid abilities without discipline requirements print their own prices: 1 or 2 DP at Novice, 3 DP at Adept, and 6 or 8 DP at Master. Every listed discipline rank must be owned before learning. No earlier card is required merely because its name or theme resembles a later one. The symbols beside a card name identify its disciplines; each discipline entry shows its symbol. Full requirements are also written out, so you never have to identify a symbol alone.

Universal actions are available to everyone. Their diamond reads U and they cost no DP, but they do not give you free equipment. The shared catalog follows by tier, alphabetically within each tier. Your class's signature choices are printed with that class. Each tier opens with a quick selection table. The tiered index at the back includes shared and class signature abilities, with requirements and page references.

Small abilities, one DP

These shared Novice abilities cost 1 DP each, require no discipline and may be purchased once each, during level 0 or later. They are not free Universal grants.

  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.7c9f1a253b6cb770]{Message by Heart}: retain one message exactly.
  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.d8a671e34b09d015]{Catch That!}: catch a falling item with your Reaction.

  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.415ad91e3af6e6c1]{Quick Exit}: gain one movement square when you Disengage.
  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c77bfa5af0bcbb7e]{Look Over Here!}: distract an adjacent attacker to aid an ally’s defense.

Read the entry in play

Check the action, attribute, targets, range and equipment. Make any choices the card requires, then pay its costs. If it calls for a roll, apply just the outcome you rolled. Track duration and limits afterward. “Once per round” resets at the start of your next turn. “Scene” means one continuous situation; a brief pause does not reset it.

Abilities can build on conditions applied by companions. An ability that targets every creature meeting a condition affects the whole eligible group within its printed range and shape. The condition remains unless the ability explicitly changes or removes it. Use player-selected activation order to set up a payoff; the target's normal condition timing still applies.

Type tags help you find abilities; they do not add rules. A card can be Attack, Magic and Control at once. Main Action, Maneuver, Reaction, Movement and Passive are separate action labels. Passive abilities cost no action unless their text says otherwise. A long activity still takes its printed full time.

Your equipment's appearance supplies the fiction. The attack supplies its mechanics. If you describe a cleaving strike with a stout walking stick, use the chosen card's range, damage and limitations. Special equipment adds its explicit effects only.

The ordinary way to attempt an activity remains available. An expert climbing card can provide better results, but you can choose an ordinary climb instead. Buying expertise gives you new options rather than forbidding everyone else from trying.

Shared card conventions

Unless a card states a limit, you may use it again by paying its action and stated costs. A free attack cannot trigger another free attack. An absent equipment grant means the ability supplies no item. Read the Gear line for specific grants and requirements; compatible abilities can share one item. These conventions apply to class signatures as well as shared abilities.

Instant effects resolve once; applied conditions use their normal duration and decay. For an area attack, make one roll using the least favorable net Boons/Banes among the targets. Apply it to each affected target. When a creature attacks an area, each affected player instead makes a defense roll. Target lines determine inclusions.

A summoning ability lets you choose an eligible profile anew each casting. Use that profile’s statistics and capabilities. The summon immediately receives one free Main command, counting as its command for that turn. Later commands cost your actions; without one it does nothing. It acts on your turn, has no independent Reactions, cannot summon, and disappears beyond 6 squares, including after forced movement. See @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.8a652a403a76d0da]{Summoned Companions} for profiles and the complete procedure.

Your hands know where each familiar piece belongs, even when you have to hurry.

Rules

Action: Varies · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: An accessible item

Drawing a weapon is included in its attack action. Dropping is free. Proper stowing or picking up costs a Maneuver. Ordinary item use follows its own card. No free two-handed grip exception is assumed.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: handle-an-item

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You pick your route and go, boots finding the next patch of open ground.

Rules

Action: Movement · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: Self

Spend up to Speed in movement squares, split around your actions. Normal terrain costs 1; difficult terrain costs 2. Occupied squares cannot be crossed unless the occupant is prone; crossing costs 2 and cannot end there.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: move

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You recognize the careless instant and strike before it passes.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None — no separate roll; resolve Basic Melee using Brawn

Target / range / shape: An adjacent creature triggering an opportunity

Make Basic Melee only; no specialty card. Leaving reach voluntarily provokes; casting, standing, stowing and retrieving are intended triggers. The start of the provoking action interrupts it: resolve this attack first, then continue the original action if the actor remains capable. Damage alone does not cancel it. Forced movement does not provoke.

Each granted Basic Melee attack uses its attacker’s Brawn and Basic Melee outcomes; this card adds no separate roll beyond any roll it explicitly requires.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: opportunity-attack

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You smother the flame, bind the cut or steady your breath, attending to the hurt before it worsens.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: Self or one adjacent creature

With a plausible method, reduce Bleeding, Burning, or Freezing by 1. This is not a general cure for all conditions. A persistent source can require a specific remedy.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: reduce-a-condition

You hunker behind your shield, listening to the hard knocks against its face.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: Self, before a defense against an attack the DA judges blockable

Requires a held shield; grants none. Gain 1 Boon to eligible defense rolls while using it. Creatures use the same rule.

Duration: Until the start of your next turn

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: shield-block

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You press against the wound and keep your voice steady, giving your friend something to hold on to.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: One adjacent Dying player character

Stabilize at 0 HP and clear death marks. No roll. This grants no HP, removes no wound, and does not restore Grit. Taking damage while stable enters Dying again.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: stabilize

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You draw a knee under yourself and rise to face what comes next.

Rules

Action: Movement · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: Self, while prone

Spend 2 squares of movement to stand. This spends movement, not a Maneuver.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: stand

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You pull the stopper and swallow the sharp mouthful, feeling warmth return to aching limbs.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None — no roll

Target / range / shape: Self or one adjacent willing creature

Requires a free hand. The giver spends the Maneuver; another recipient spends a Reaction unless at 0 HP. Restore the bottle’s printed fixed HP, apply Life resistance with minimum 1 actual healing where HP is missing, then check inventory. No outcome roll. Potions do not restore the dead or end Last Words.

Duration: Instant

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: Universal · DP: Not purchased · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Universal

Limits: Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

ID: use-a-healing-potion

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions} · Catalog

You name what your enemy stands to lose and flick a glowing coal toward them. Their answer dies as the ember flares.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Guile

Target / range / shape: One visible enemy within 5 squares.

Make a Guile spell attack. You are the source of its Frightened condition.

  • Weak: 3 fire damage.
  • Standard: 3 fire damage and Frightened 1.
  • Strong: 5 fire damage and Frightened 1.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Flame 1

Type: Magic / Attack / Control

ID: a-coal-for-a-promise

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You dip your head as if making room for a reply. The blade comes up before the greeting can be returned.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Guile

Target / range / shape: One adjacent enemy.

Make a Guile melee attack. If you began Hidden, gain 1 Boon to the attack.

  • Weak: 3 physical damage.
  • Standard: 3 physical damage and Slowed 1.
  • Strong: 5 physical damage and Slowed 2.

Equipment / acquisition: Use an ordinary melee weapon (Bulk 1), supplied on learning if needed.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Subterfuge 1

Type: Skill / Attack / Control

ID: a-courtesy-unanswered

pages.name: A Door That Is Not There

text.content:
You draw a latch in the air. Weathered wood settles around it, complete with the faint sway of a hanging curtain.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied square within 4 squares.

Create a silent flat image of a door, window, curtain or screen in the chosen square for ten minutes. It may include small natural movement and remains while you move. Physical contact reveals the image's illusory nature. You may end it freely or replace it with a new casting.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Mind 1

Type: Magic / Utility

ID: a-door-that-is-not-there

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You feel the wind fall quiet beneath the ridge and find the dry hollow where last year's leaves still lie.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Time: Ten minutes of examination.

Target / range / shape: One campsite you can examine.

After examining the site, learn the environmental dangers that the site currently presents and an available way to shelter from each. When your party makes camp using that shelter, you and up to six companions gain 1 Boon to attribute rolls against weather and exposure while that camp remains in use.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Wilderness 1

Type: Skill / Utility

ID: a-good-place-to-stop

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

A hand like your grandmother's closes over your companion's shoulder. The blow passes, and the hand guides them to your side.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible willing ally within 2 squares, before it defends against a physical attack.

The ally gains 1 Boon to the defense. After the attack resolves, it may move up to 2 squares without provoking to a free square adjacent to you.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Defense / Movement

ID: a-hand-from-before

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You tie the knot without looking and test it with a sharp pull. Then you put your friend's weight on it.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: A rope you hold and a reachable suitable anchor during a climb.

During a climb, secure or release a held rope at a suitable anchor you reach as part of the climb, without a separate action.

Equipment / acquisition: A free hand; one ordinary rope coil (Bulk 1), supplied on learning if needed.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Athletics 1

Type: Skill / Utility

ID: a-knot-you-can-trust

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You lift your instrument, find the room's rhythm, and let the first phrase carry your argument.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: Self, while playing your chosen instrument.

When you learn this ability, choose one ordinary instrument you own, such as a lute, flute, drum, fiddle or horn. While you play that instrument, gain 1 Boon to any Guile roll. The instrument must be in your hands and in playing condition. The Boon can support performance, persuasion, deception and other Guile approaches that the music carries. Ordinary performance remains available to everyone; a performance with no uncertain consequence needs no roll.

Duration: While you play the chosen instrument.

Equipment / acquisition: Requires an ordinary Musical Instrument (Bulk 1), chosen when you learn this ability; grants none.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 1 · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Utility

Tags: Universal / Skill / Social / Passive

Limits: Purchase once; choose one instrument when learned.

ID: a-party-piece

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You trade a little news from the road, remember a name, and make room for someone else beside the fire. Before long, someone is making room for you.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Time: Ten minutes sharing conversation or news.

Target / range / shape: A nonhostile gathering whose members can understand you.

After the conversation, the DA introduces a willing local host who offers your party an ordinary meal and a place to sleep until the next morning. The host also points you toward one local person who can help with your stated business.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Influence 1

Type: Skill / Utility

Limits: Once per visit to a community.

ID: a-place-at-any-fire

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You draw a bright stroke across the air. It spreads in front of your companion just as the blow arrives.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: Self or one visible willing ally within 3 squares before a defense roll.

The target gains 1 Boon to the defense.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Guard 1

Type: Magic / Defense

ID: a-sign-against-harm

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

pages.name: A Thought That Is Not Yours

text.content:
You hold your enemy's gaze and let one impossible shape pass between you. Their next movement loses its place in the world.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Reason

Target / range / shape: One visible enemy within 4 squares.

Make a Reason spell attack.

  • Weak: 2 mental damage.
  • Standard: 3 mental damage and Dazed 1.
  • Strong: 5 mental damage and Dazed 1.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Mind 1

Type: Magic / Attack / Control

ID: a-thought-that-is-not-yours

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You strike the first line of the marching song. Your companion answers with a step forward and a grin they had almost forgotten.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One willing ally within 3 squares who hears you.

The ally may move 1 square without provoking and gains 1 Boon to its next attribute roll before the start of your next turn.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Influence 1

Type: Skill

ID: a-verse-for-courage

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You extend a hand as if asking for a dance. An unseen tug supplies the first step before the invitation can be answered.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: Guile

Target / range / shape: One visible enemy within 4 squares.

Make a Guile control attack.

  • Weak: Pull the target 1 square toward you.
  • Standard: Pull it 1 square toward you; you may move 1 square without provoking.
  • Strong: Pull it 2 squares toward you; you may move 1 square without provoking.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Mind 1

Type: Magic / Control / Movement

ID: an-invitation-elsewhere

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You watch the uneven stride, wait for the weight to shift, and put your blade where the armor has to bend.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Knowledge

Target / range / shape: One adjacent enemy.

Make a Knowledge melee attack.

  • Weak: 3 physical damage.
  • Standard: 3 physical damage; learn the target's physical resistance.
  • Strong: 5 physical damage; learn the target's physical resistance and move 1 square without provoking.

Equipment / acquisition: Use an ordinary melee weapon (Bulk 1), supplied on learning if needed.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Scholarship 1

Type: Skill / Attack / Utility

ID: anatomy-of-an-opening

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You answer the stranger in the language of their childhood, and hear their surprise give way to recognition.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: Self

When you learn this ability, choose one ordinary language you do not already know. You can speak and understand it, and read and write its usual script if it has one. Record the language on your sheet. A signed language uses signing instead of speech. Choose from the campaign's ordinary languages with the DA. Secret and supernatural languages are learned through their own paths.

Duration: Permanent knowledge of the chosen language.

Equipment / acquisition: None.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 1 · Requirements to learn: None

Type: Utility

Tags: Universal / Skill / Passive

Limits: Purchase once; choose one language when learned.

ID: another-tongue

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You close your palm over the flames. Their heat gathers into a tiny coal that crumbles between your fingers.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: Self, one adjacent willing creature, or one adjacent hand-sized ordinary flame.

Reduce temporary Burning by 2. You may also extinguish an ordinary unattended flame small enough to cover with your hand.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Flame 1

Type: Magic / Recovery / Utility

ID: bank-the-embers

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

The blow rocks you back a step. You bare your teeth, plant your heel, and answer with the whole weight of your body.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Fortitude

Target / range / shape: One adjacent creature.

Make a Fortitude melee attack.

  • Weak: 3 physical damage.
  • Standard: 5 physical damage.
  • Strong: 7 physical damage.

Equipment / acquisition: Use an ordinary melee weapon (Bulk 1), supplied on learning if needed.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Arms 1

Type: Skill / Attack

ID: blood-in-the-teeth

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You whisper into your cupped hand. The same words emerge from the empty stairwell in the voice everyone expected to hear.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One point within 4 squares with an open path for sound.

Create one brief nonverbal sound or speak a phrase of up to twenty words from the chosen point, using your own voice or a voice you have heard.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Mind 1

Type: Magic / Utility

ID: borrow-a-voice

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

Fur rises along your arms. You drop to all fours, and the scent of the fleeing creature parts from the smells of rain and earth.

Rules

Action: Maneuver · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: Self.

Become a wolf, great cat, boar or similar one-square land beast for the scene. Gain 1 Boon to rolls following a trail by scent. Equipment folds into the form and supplies its benefits again when you return. To speak, cast spells or use carried items, return to your own shape with a Maneuver.

Claw or bite: Main Action, Brawn; one adjacent enemy.

  • Weak: 3 physical damage.
  • Standard: 3 physical damage; push 1 square.
  • Strong: 5 physical damage; push 1 square and apply Prone.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Wilderness 1

Type: Magic / Attack / Utility

ID: borrow-the-beast

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You adjust the collar and practice the little habit that makes the clothes look lived in. Then you join the room as if you have always belonged.

Rules

Action: Passive · Attribute: None (no roll)

Time: Ten minutes of preparation.

Target / range / shape: One mundane disguise and plausible role.

Prepare a plausible role with suitable clothing. Learn one observable detail or habit that helps sell it. While maintaining that disguise, gain 1 Boon to Guile rolls passing as the role.

Equipment / acquisition: Suitable clothing.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Subterfuge 1

Type: Skill / Utility

ID: borrowed-clothes-borrowed-manners

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You lean into your harness and let every strap take its part of the blow.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: Fortitude

Target / range / shape: Self while armored, before Stability is applied to forced movement against you.

Make a Fortitude roll.

  • Weak: Gain Stability 1 against the forced movement.
  • Standard: Gain Stability 2 against it.
  • Strong: Gain Stability 3 against it.

Equipment / acquisition: Worn armor.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Armor 1

Type: Skill / Defense

ID: braced-harness

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

Heat gathers behind your teeth. You open your mouth, and a low stream of flame races across the ground.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Fortitude

Target / range / shape: Every creature in three contiguous squares in a straight line beginning adjacent to you.

Make a Fortitude line spell attack.

  • Weak: 3 fire damage.
  • Standard: 3 fire damage and Burning 1.
  • Strong: 5 fire damage and Burning 1.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Flame 1

Type: Magic / Attack / Control

ID: breath-of-the-wyrmling

Build this character · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You exhale white mist. It rolls over nearby weapons and leaves a shining crust on every lash and collar.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: Knowledge

Target / range / shape: Every creature in three connected squares, all adjacent to you.

Make a Knowledge area spell attack.

  • Weak: 2 cold damage.
  • Standard: 3 cold damage.
  • Strong: 4 cold damage and Freezing 1.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Frost 1

Type: Magic / Attack / Control

ID: breath-of-white

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You whistle once. A hound-shaped shimmer lifts its head, catches your scent, and waits for the chase.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied placement within 3 squares that fits the chosen form's entire footprint.

Choose one Animal entry from the summon selection with a minimum tier of 1 or lower. Call one instance using its summon profile. Choose the form anew each casting. It remains for one scene.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Summoning

ID: call-the-faithful-hound

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You sketch a joint in the air. Another locks into place, and a little machine unfolds around your hand.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied placement within 3 squares that fits the chosen form's entire footprint.

Choose one Construct entry from the summon selection with a minimum tier of 1 or lower. Call one instance using its summon profile. Choose the form anew each casting. It remains for one scene.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Summoning

ID: summon-construct-novice

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

A spark, a drop or a pebble circles your palm. You give it a name, and it unfolds into a restless little shape.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied placement within 3 squares that fits the chosen form's entire footprint.

Choose one Elemental entry from the summon selection with a minimum tier of 1 or lower. Call one instance using its summon profile. Choose the form anew each casting. It remains for one scene.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Summoning

ID: summon-elemental-novice

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You open your hand as if offering a secret. A small, bright figure steps from the space between your fingers.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied placement within 3 squares that fits the chosen form's entire footprint.

Choose one Fey entry from the summon selection with a minimum tier of 1 or lower. Call one instance using its summon profile. Choose the form anew each casting. It remains for one scene.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Summoning

ID: a-friend-beneath-the-door

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You speak into the hush between breaths. A little light answers, wearing the outline of something remembered.

Rules

Action: Main Action · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One visible unoccupied placement within 3 squares that fits the chosen form's entire footprint.

Choose one Spirit entry from the summon selection with a minimum tier of 1 or lower. Call one instance using its summon profile. Choose the form anew each casting. It remains for one scene.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Calling 1

Type: Magic / Summoning

ID: call-a-burrower

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You call the name their oldest friend would use. Their eyes find yours through the panic, and their breathing begins to slow.

Rules

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One willing ally within 3 squares who hears you, before an attribute roll penalized by Frightened.

Reduce the ally's temporary Frightened by 1 before its roll.

---

Tier / minimum level: 1 · DP: 2 · Requirements to learn: Influence 1

Type: Skill / Recovery

ID: call-their-name

@UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c0c043f22d65aa20]{Card conventions}

You draw a pale line through the air. Spectral bones settle around it, then lift their empty gaze to you.

Rules

A coil of rope is easy to overlook until someone is hanging above a ravine. Choose equipment for the journey you expect, leave room for what you might find, and know which hand will reach your potion when the fight goes badly.

HOL uses one currency: coins. A listed price buys the described ordinary item or full supply. Training, discipline ranks and signature access are purchased through character development, not coins. Owning armor does not teach you to use its gated capabilities.

Useful intact gear sells for half its listed value, rounded down, or trades at full value with a willing trader. A 12-coin weapon sells for 6 or trades for 12 coins of goods. Pay any shortfall in coins; excess trade value is not cash change. A merchant does not have unlimited stock or an obligation to buy everything you make.

A coil of rope is easy to overlook until someone is hanging above a ravine. Choose equipment for the journey you expect, leave room for what you might find, and know which hand will reach your potion when the fight goes badly.

Coins and trade

HOL uses one currency: coins. A listed price buys the described ordinary item or full supply. Training, discipline ranks and signature access are purchased through character development, not coins. Owning armor does not teach you to use its gated capabilities.

Useful intact gear sells for half its listed value, rounded down, or trades at full value with a willing trader. A 12-coin weapon sells for 6 or trades for 12 coins of goods. Pay any shortfall in coins; excess trade value is not cash change. A merchant does not have unlimited stock or an obligation to buy everything you make.

Armor and training

Choose armor you have learned to wear. Each training grants one ordinary matching suit, Bulk 1, if you do not already own one. Its resistance applies only while wearing that armor. Buying a suit with coins grants neither training nor resistance.

Novice training can be granted or purchased during level-0 creation. Buy discipline ranks in order, but you do not need a lower-tier armor training card to learn a higher one. Matching resistances use the highest value, normally capped at 3.

Bulk and hands

Record each carried item's Bulk. Most individual equipment entries and supply bundles use 1 Bulk; the entry tells you otherwise. A pack adds its own Bulk and does not erase its contents. Capacity is 10 + 3 × Brawn. Each Bulk above capacity reduces Speed by 1, to a minimum of 0.

A single compatible weapon serves all the attacks that can use it. Ordinary weapon appearance changes no mechanics. A flaming melee weapon can add its printed fire effect to a compatible attack; it cannot become a ranged weapon simply because you chose a ranged card.

Track occupied hands. Healing requires a free hand. A bow, two-handed weapon, or weapon-and-shield combination leaves none. Drawing for an attack is part of that attack, dropping is free, and proper stowing or picking up costs a Maneuver. There is no automatic free grip-change exception.

Inventory dice

A supply bundle has an inventory die instead of a counted number of uses. After using it, roll that die. On a 1, reduce it one step. On any other result it stays where it is. The use you just completed still works.

d20 → d12 → d10 → d8 → d6 → d4 → out

Check at the interval printed on the supply: ammunition when used, food by its person-day rule, lighting by its hour, and so on. A d4 healing bottle has a one-in-four chance of becoming empty after each use. It is not a promise of four doses.

> Example — the last swallow. You drink a lesser healing bottle and restore its > 6 HP, reduced by Life resistance if applicable. Then roll its d4 inventory die. > A 1 empties the bottle; you still received that healing. At full HP the bottle > cannot heal beyond your maximum.

Recipes raise an existing supply by their permitted number of steps, up to the recipe's cap. A store refill uses the listed policy. Do not turn unknown leftovers into additional full bottles by splitting them among containers.

Special equipment and understanding

A special item adds only the effects it prints: damage, resistance, an ability or another explicit benefit. Apply normal nonstacking rules to matching numerical bonuses. Different damage-type resistances can coexist; use the highest of each.

The item states whether understanding is required. Identification abilities reveal different kinds of information. Knowing a recipe is a separate permission from knowing what an item does. The recipe section lists tools, materials, time and what the crafting result produces; none of those are supplied by the recipe's name alone.

All prices are whole coins, with no metal denominations. Prices establish a usable town market, not a historical currency conversion. Use the prices and supply rules below.

What a coin buys

A simple meal costs 1 coin. A plain bed costs 2 coins per night, meals separate. Ordinary local labor pays about 3 coins per day; skilled work about 6. These are anchors, not a requirement to simulate wages. Dangerous adventuring earns more because it risks wounds, scarce Grit and death, not because food becomes expensive when a character gains levels.

Equipment grants still happen first. Coins buy objects and supplies, never DP, discipline ranks, signature access or training. Owning armor does not grant its training card. A purchased weapon’s appearance supplies no damage modifier. Prices for functionally equivalent ordinary melee weapons are equal; a jeweled hilt may be valuable decoration but does not hit harder.

Price list

The linked item is the source for its price, use and Bulk. Most entries are Bulk 1. A worn plain outfit is the explicit exception; an extra outfit is Bulk 1. Containers add their own Bulk and never reduce their contents’ Bulk.

Supplies and restocking

The printed price buys one full supply at its listed die, including an ordinary holder. All three healing bottles currently use d4; their potency, not supply die, differs. This pass preserves those existing values rather than quietly increasing potion longevity. A die checks after use and on 1 steps down; the last use works.

A d4 averages 4 uses before empty; d6 averages 10 total uses through its d4 stage; d8 averages 18. These are expectations, not guaranteed charges. The inventory die cannot be converted into an exact number of arrows or spoonfuls.

Shop refills: a shop can refill a supply to its printed starting die for its full listed supply price. Or buy a separate full supply at that price, which costs another Bulk. No discounted partial refill, die combining, decanting into fresh full-die bottles or cash credit for unknown leftovers. This keeps the market simple without changing crafting’s existing step-increase procedure. Fresh safe water can refill its flask freely; a town refill costs 1 coin if charged.

Availability, selling and crafting

These prices assume a supplied town. Ordinary travel goods are common. Specialist tools, potions and unusual supplies need an appropriate seller. Special equipment prices are valuation benchmarks: the DA decides whether an item is actually on sale. No automatic stock refresh after a rest or new scene.

For an unusual shortage or remote seller, the DA may quote double ordinary prices; otherwise use the printed value rather than maintaining regional multipliers. Record a concrete offer before buying. Exact scarcity and merchant stock remain adventure decisions, not a universal cap on player purchases.

Agreed sale/trade rule: intact, useful gear sells for half list price, rounded down, or trades for its full listed value with a willing trader. A 12-coin weapon sells for 6 coins or trades for 12 coins of goods. Pay any shortfall in coins; unused trade value is not cash change. A trade cannot be redeemed for coins, vouchers or other cash equivalents at full value. Card-granted items use the same rule, and selling never renews their grant. Consumables and materials with uncertain remaining supply have no standard resale offer. Goods freshly crafted or acquired at full supply may attract half-price offers, but the buyer must actually need that quantity. Special items still require an available willing trader; apply the same half-sale/full-trade rule to the agreed item valuation. Treasure such as gems has its stated trade value, without a second automatic half-price reduction.

All material bundles must name their actual contents. Ordinary d6 ingredients cost 12 coins; a d6 prepared healing-ingredient bundle costs 80. Other rare inputs need a quote. Materials must meet the recipe: a common bundle cannot become life salts by relabeling it. Recipes are still found, derived or granted through cards, not automatically available for coin purchase.

Crafting remains useful. Gathering ingredients, knowing recipes and spending time can save coins. This is not a closed or proven macroeconomy: foraging success, recipe yields, local demand and available downtime determine profit. A merchant’s willing purchase is not an infinite exchange machine. Large production should be reviewed before assigning guaranteed commercial income.

Shopping bundles and starting range

Bundles are convenience lists at the exact sum of their parts, with no discount or Bulk exemption. Each person still chooses what to carry.

  • Road essentials: 24 coins, 5 Bulk. Pack 3 + sleeping roll 4 + filled water

flask 3 + d8 food 9 + d6 lighting 5. One plain worn outfit is free.

  • Self-contained explorer: 31 coins, 7 Bulk. Road essentials + rope 5 and small

necessities 2. At Brawn −1, this alone fills capacity 7.

  • Road essentials plus lesser healing: 44 coins, 6 Bulk. Add a 20-coin d4 bottle.
  • Explorer plus lesser healing: 51 coins, 8 Bulk. Useful, but too much for a

Brawn −1 character without sharing a load or accepting a Speed penalty.

A spell light can replace a purchased lighting supply if the group accepts its limitations. Sharing rope, light and camp tools is a choice, not a free group inventory. Card-granted items remain part of carried Bulk even though they cost no coins at creation.

Agreed starting target: 50–70 coins after card grants. At 50, a character can buy road essentials, a lesser potion and retain 6 coins; at 70 that same choice leaves 26 for specialist purchases or reserves. A recipe is the knowledge of how to make a particular thing. It tells you which crafting ability permits the work, what tools and materials you need, how long an attempt takes, and what the result produces. Knowing a recipe does not supply its ingredients or grant the ability needed to use it.

Read the entry before beginning. A project may accumulate progress toward a completion target; a supply recipe may instead raise an existing inventory die. Follow the printed outcomes and limits. Starting crafting abilities provide their stated recipe choices; you can learn further compatible recipes through the appropriate ability or discover them during play.

Granted by tells you how a recipe enters your repertoire. Used with lists abilities that can carry out its work. Ordinary Recipe Study grants two compatible recipes, but you must already know an ability that can use them.

For every recipe, roll the crafting ability’s printed attribute at the end of an attempt. Work alone; there is no group crafting. Accumulate project progress until you meet the completion target.
