You call across a boundary, and something answers: paws on stone, a flicker of ancestral light, a shape unfolding from cold air. The creature acts through your attention. Its presence gives you choices, not a second independent turn.

Choose from the profiles in this chapter when a summoning ability permits the category and tier. Higher-tier cards can choose eligible lower-tier creatures. Category names alone do not grant access to an unlisted creature.

Summons are energy forms shaped to resemble creatures. They cannot receive healing and disappear at 0 HP without leaving a body. They occupy squares, block movement, take damage and can be pushed or grappled normally unless the profile says otherwise; energy form grants no automatic incorporeality or immunity.

Command the creature

Spend your Main Action to give one summon a Main Action and a Maneuver. Spend your Maneuver to give one summon a Maneuver and movement. Normal conversions apply. The Main-command package has no separate movement allowance: convert its Maneuver to movement if it needs to approach before attacking.

A summon receives at most one command on your turn. You can spend your Main Action on one creature and your Maneuver on another. A summoning card's immediate free Main command counts as that creature's command for the turn.

Summoned creatures require your constant interaction and concentration to maintain their presence in reality. At the end of your turn, each of your summons that received no command during that turn disappears. Its immediate command when summoned counts for that turn.

An uncommanded summon does nothing. It does not follow, keep watch, alert you, continue a previous task, or take Reactions and opportunity attacks. Existing conditions, durations and passive defenses still operate. Resolve its turn-based timing on your turn. You cannot summon creatures that summon more creatures.

Keep the connection

A summon disappears beyond 6 squares from you, including after forced movement of either participant. It also disappears at 0 HP, or when you become unconscious or die. Its duration may end earlier. It leaves no permanent equipment or loot.

Measure the tether between the nearest occupied squares of controller and summon, using ordinary grid distance. At 6 squares the summon remains; beyond 6 it immediately disappears. The nearest square of a large form sets the distance.

Healing through a summon

When a summon uses a printed healing ability, you pay its HP cost once before resolution, bypassing resistance. You must remain above 0 HP after payment. The summon uses its own attribute and outcomes and still requires its command and action. It can heal an eligible other creature, but cannot receive healing. Ordinary unsummoned healers pay their own cost.

Give a useful order

“Attack that creature,” “defend this spot,” “move into cover,” and “help them cross” are clear intentions. The creature still needs the printed capability and enough commanded actions to carry them out. A previous order never buys activity next turn. Outside combat, you must continue directing a longer task for its full time.

Roll the creature's attack attribute, not your own, and read its player-facing attacker outcomes. When it is attacked, roll the defense attribute named by the incoming attack using the creature's value. Apply the profile's attack or defense Boons/Banes and resistance normally. There is never a second opposed roll.

The profiles below include only the summoned form's permitted capabilities. A monster's dramatic description does not grant its summoned form extra actions, active auras, independent attacks or skills.

Choose a creature, not another spell

The summoning card specifies category, maximum eligible tier, number, placement and duration. Choose an explicitly eligible bestiary entry each casting. The six families are Animal, Fey, Spirit, Elemental, Undead and Construct; each has independent Novice, Adept and Master cards. Higher cards may select eligible lower-tier entries. All eighteen currently summon one creature. More powerful tiers expand eligibility, not the number of independent actors. No prerequisite-card chains.

A category is an explicit bestiary tag. A ghost is not automatically selectable under both Spirit and Undead; its entry must say so. These are summoned forms, not permission to seize an existing creature or extract permanent equipment.

Summoned energy forms — approved October 16, 2026

A summon is shaped from energies to resemble and act like the chosen creature; it is not an actual physical creature brought into the scene. It cannot be healed. Its HP tracks how much damage the form can sustain. At 0 HP it disappears rather than leaving a body. The existing duration, tether and controller-disappearance rules still apply.

Tangibility — approved October 16, 2026: summoned forms occupy squares and block movement normally. They can take damage and be pushed or grappled normally unless their card explicitly says otherwise. Being made from energy does not automatically make a summon incorporeal or grant damage or control immunities.

This restriction concerns receiving healing. A summon with a printed healing ability can still heal an eligible other creature, with its controller paying the printed cost as described below. Ordinary unsummoned creatures keep their own healing rules. A printed harmful Life effect is damage, not healing.

Pay for activity

Summoned creatures require your constant interaction and concentration to maintain their presence in reality. At the end of your turn, each of your summons that received no command during that turn disappears. The immediate command granted when you summon a creature counts as its command for that turn.

Agreed: an uncommanded summon does nothing. It does not follow, keep watch, alert its controller, continue attacking, search, help or perform a standing order. It takes no independent Reaction, including an opportunity attack. A prior order never pays for another turn. Outside combat the same rule prevents unattended work, scouting or guard duty; the controller must actively spend the required time and actions directing it.

  • Controller spends Main Action: one summon receives Main Action + Maneuver.
  • Controller spends Maneuver: one summon receives Maneuver + movement.
  • A summon receives at most one command on the controller’s turn. The controller

may spend these two actions on different summons.

  • Normal conversions apply: Main → Maneuver → movement. There is no separate free

movement grant in the Main-command package. For example, convert its Maneuver to movement to approach, then spend Main on an attack.

  • A newly summoned creature receives the summoning card’s immediate free Main

command. That is its command for this turn; it cannot also receive a paid one.

  • Resolve the granted activity on the controller’s turn. It cannot be banked for

an enemy turn. No summon chains and no independent summon turns.

Commanding has no roll. Any permitted attack or task uses the summon profile’s printed procedure. A command is not automatic success or a way to invent a skill.

Healing through a summon — approved October 16, 2026

When a summoned creature uses a healing ability, its controller pays the ability’s printed HP cost instead of the summon. Pay once, before resolving the ability, bypassing resistance. The controller must remain above 0 HP after payment or the ability cannot be used. The summon still uses its own printed attribute and healing outcomes; its command and action requirements are unchanged.

For example, the Moon Hart’s Battle Mending costs its controller 3 HP, then the player rolls the hart’s Reason for 5/10/15 healing. The hart does not also pay 3 HP. An ordinary unsummoned healer continues to pay its own cost.

Orders in ordinary language

These examples describe intent, not a new menu of abilities granted to every creature.

OrderExecution within the paid package
Attack that creatureUse a permitted attack. A Main command can convert its Maneuver to movement to approach first.
Defend that spotA Maneuver command supplies movement and Defend, if the profile permits Defend. It does not grant free attacks at intruders.
Move there / follow meUse only the granted movement, with legal routes and endpoints. Following stops when that movement ends.
Move and hideMove to real concealment, then use the profile’s printed hiding action if the remaining budget permits it. No automatic Hidden.
Move and keep watchMove, then use its printed observation action if affordable. It can report what it notices during that commanded activity; no continuing lookout afterward.
Help themUse Aid or a printed support ability, if permitted and affordable.
Fetch or handle thisUse permitted movement and interaction; anatomy, reach, carried Bulk and action costs still apply.
Track thisUse the profile’s tracking procedure and available senses. The command does not grant tracking expertise.

If a creature lacks the required capability or the package lacks the necessary actions, it cannot complete that order. A longer task needs continued commands and the printed activity time; one spoken instruction never buys hours of labor.

What still happens without a command

Until it disappears at the end of your turn, the creature remains present and can be damaged or forcibly moved. Existing conditions, durations, tether checks and already-resolved effects continue normally. These are consequences, not permission for new activity. A previous Defend benefit lasts only to its printed expiry; it does not renew itself.

Six-square tether — approved October 16, 2026

Measure ordinary grid distance between the nearest occupied squares of the controller and summon. Diagonals count normally as one square. The summon remains present at a distance of 6 squares; if the nearest distance exceeds 6, it immediately disappears. Voluntary or forced movement of either participant can break the tether.

For example, a large summon remains present with its nearest square 6 squares away and its farthest square 7 away. If its nearest square becomes 7 squares away, it disappears. Neither creature’s center nor farthest occupied square sets the distance.

The summon profile must anchor any “your turn” duration or condition tick to the controller’s turn. Passive defenses such as resistance remain applicable. Do not import automatic attacks, active auras or triggered abilities from a monster entry without an explicit summon-profile procedure consistent with command-only activity.

Bestiary selection

The summon selection provides 73 entries, covering all six categories at tiers 1, 3 and 7. Each prints HP, all six attributes, attack and target-defense attributes, movement, footprint, senses, resistance, the no-healing rule, command options and restrictions. Category or CV alone never authorizes a creature.

The creature procedure and summon selection document the permitted command activities. Use the approved tether measurement above and the @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.3292b6a49dcf7236]{moving-group placement rules} where relevant. Use the entry itself, not a monster’s narrative tactics as a standing order. No activity, alerts or independent Reactions without the permitted command.

Latest agreement: summons disappear when their controller becomes unconscious or dies. Players roll their creatures’ printed attack and defense attributes; see @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.f5003d6e49eeed0c]{session resolution}.

Designer-reviewed working entries consolidated from the design discussion in issue #1125. These replace the compact placeholder table. They have not been balance simulated. Numerical fixtures and their comparative balance remain subject to tests.

Procedure and notation

Use the wound roll in @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.9303127ab1b28c3b]{recovery}: retain the highest three dice, sort lowest to highest, and read the result. There are 56 possible entries per table: 21 in the 100 band, 15 in 200, 10 in 300, 6 in 400, 3 in 500, and only 666 in 600.

Select the damage type that dealt the most damage after resistance; the player chooses on a tie. Physical includes sonic and force. Fire, Cold, and Lightning use Elemental; Mental, Radiant, and Life/Necrotic each have their own table. This shared Elemental table does not merge the individual elemental resistances.

If every damage component is reduced to zero and the minimum 1 total damage causes a wound, the player chooses among the attack's original damage types.

Example: an attack deals 2 Physical and 1 Fire damage, both fully resisted. Its minimum 1 damage drops the character to 0 HP. The player chooses the Physical or Elemental wound table.

If the body part is absent or the injury does not apply, move down to the next valid listed result until an applicable entry is reached (for example 116 → 122). Every table ends in 666, Last Words. Players choose source-appropriate descriptions with the DA; existing choices of comparable injury remain subject to applicability.

Immediate consequences happen once: push, pull, and knockdown are not recurring wound effects. Use existing forced movement, terrain, and collision rules. The DA chooses a direction consistent with the injury. A push followed by Prone can be described as a throw; no separate airborne throw mechanic is introduced here.

Temporary conditions use @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.b8dbac21301a8aa3]{conditions}: resolve end-of-turn effects, then decrease by 1. No entry uses a separate short-duration Dazed or Paralyzed rule. An asterisk prevents automatic decay. Blinded and Deafened have one effect; their numbers measure duration, not severity. Lasting movement penalties and Banes remain until their printed remedy, rather than decaying as if they were conditions. The DA decides when a Bane to physical or mental activities applies.

Treatment: one attempt per wound per day, even with several healers. Weak / Standard / Strong adds 1/2/3 cumulative progress. Meet or exceed the Recovery Value (RV) to remove the listed lasting effect. Progress remains with the wound. A dash means no treatment track, not an automatic healing roll. Temporary conditions end by decay or their normal remedies; treatment does not itself extinguish or staunch them. One treatment track resolves the listed treatable effects of one wound.

Example: Physical 333 applies Bleeding 1 and a lasting Bane. Bleeding can decay or be reduced by an appropriate Main Action; it does not recur because the wound remains. Soft Tissue treatment reaching RV 3 removes the Bane. The scar still counts.

All wounds leave scars that permanently count toward future wound rolls. Cosmetic wounds need no treatment. Where treatment softens a socially significant scar, it removes both the intimidation Boon and persuasion Bane, not just the drawback. Rest alternatives must be printed explicitly; there is no universal rest timer.

Treatment capabilities supplied by the current card catalog: Soft Tissue Treatment, Bone Treatment, Elemental Wound Treatment, Mental Wound Treatment, Radiant Wound Treatment, Life Wound Treatment. These are broad capabilities, not a separate ability for each injury. The treatment cards print their attributes, discipline requirements, costs and time. Treatment is limited to one attempt per wound per day, with 1/2/3 progress by outcome.

Treatment cannot regrow a lost body part. An artificial limb or explicitly restorative ability specifies what it remedies. Scars remain even after functional recovery. Physical wounds leave minor scars in 100–200, moderate scars in 300–400, and major scars in 500. Mental scars do not dictate personality, allegiance, or choices. Elemental scars are visibly more pronounced, including at low severity.

Open test concerns: wounds usually occur while Dying, so immediate Dazed or Paralyzed may matter most after prompt healing. Burning/Freezing are resistible; Bleeding is not. Frightened depends on a perceptible source. These differences need testing, not an assumption that equal ratings create equal danger.

Action: Reaction · Attribute: None (no roll)

Target / range / shape: One adjacent willing ally, after a single-target attack is declared against it but before rolling.

Duration: The triggering attack.

Equipment / acquisition: None.

Signature limit: Repeatable; uses your Reaction.

Hook and Drive holds a doorway; Step Between lets Borin swap squares with an ally and take a single-target attack before the roll. Taking prisoners is a deliberate use of Take Them Alive. Pip, Oren and Vaelis use the 1-DP shared abilities to spend their odd creation points.

All start at full HP, Grit 2, no wounds and no death marks. Unspent creation DP expires separately at each stage. Ancestry and culture are independent: Mara is a human of Forest Communities, and Oren is a human raised in Deep Halls.

What was checked

  • All attributes are −2 through +2, total +3, and satisfy the chosen class minima.
  • Each origin pair exists in its source. Only those rank-1 grants qualify level-0

purchases; no class rank or purchased rank is borrowed from level 1.

  • Every purchased card is Novice. Requirements are held before each purchase;

class-granted disciplines are valid and distinct. Duplicate ranks yield 1 DP each at the correct stage, never rank 2.

  • Class Home/Adjacent/Foreign prices and all running balances were checked.
  • All six signatures belong to the chosen class and level. No extra signature

purchases or advanced-tier cards are assumed.

  • HP, Speed, capacity and carried Bulk were recomputed. Each item is traced to an

explicit grant; compatible duplicate grants are counted once. Described weapons use the cards’ mechanics, not statistics imported from their appearance.

  • Oren’s six recipe choices are distinct and compatible. Recipe knowledge does not

supply ingredients or finished products. Other characters have no recipe grants.

These checks were run against the source Markdown with a temporary validation script and followed by a reading of the sheets. The normal catalog audit also passes. This checks these six builds, not every possible creation route. All purchased disciplines here are rank 1: buying deeper ranks without access to higher-tier cards did not serve these particular concepts.

At the table

These examples show particular choices, not compulsory builds. Lira remains a Blade archer; the Warden is another option for a dedicated wilderness hunter. Pip fights with Guile, Oren with Knowledge, and Mara can heal or change form.

Borin’s weapon and shield and Lira’s bow leave no free potion hand. Equipment, materials, coins and Bulk are recorded in each shopping ledger. Recipe knowledge does not create supplies. Creation DP remainders expire at each stage.

These six examples do not establish comparative class strength or encounter CV.

Your turn in order

1. Resolve any start-of-turn instructions. If Dying, choose Grit or a death roll. 2. Refresh your turn budget. If Dazed or Grappled, choose the action categories you retain. 3. Move and take permitted actions in your chosen order. Declare an ability before rolling. 4. Resolve end-of-turn conditions, then reduce temporary numbered ratings by 1. 5. Mark continuing effects and keep your available Reaction ready for its trigger.

Quick rules

SituationRule
Ordinary roll3d6 + one attribute; Weak ≤8, Standard 9–14, Strong ≥15
Boons / BanesCancel; add up to 3 net dice; keep highest / lowest 3
Natural 111 / 666Weak + complication / Strong + benefit, using retained dice
InitiativeOne unmodified 3d6; 12+ players first; same side begins each round
Action conversionMain → Maneuver → movement; never upward
Ordinary movementNormal 1; difficult 2; diagonal 1; stand costs 2
Occupied spaceCross only if occupant Prone, cost 2; never end there
CoverPartial 1 Bane; heavy 3 Banes; no path means no attack
ResistanceHighest matching type, cap 3; minimum 1 damage per event
StabilityDefault 0; highest explicit grant, cap 3; deduct once per new creature
Free attacksSpend no actions; never trigger more free attacks
Healing spell costNovice 1, Adept 3, Master 7 HP; pay first, stay above 0

Glossary

Ability. A learned technique, spell, talent or other capability with its own procedure. “Card” refers to that rules entry, whether printed on a card or in this book.

Action. Something a character chooses to do. An action can call for a roll; a roll itself is not an extra action. A Main Action is a specific part of the turn budget.

Attribute. One of Brawn, Fortitude, Agility, Guile, Knowledge or Reason. Add only the attribute called for by the action or DA.

Benefit. A useful additional advantage, including the extra consequence of a natural 666. Apply the stated Strong outcome as well.

Boon / Bane. An extra die that changes which three dice you retain. Boons and Banes cancel before applying their net cap.

Bulk. An item's inventory load. Capacity and carried Bulk determine encumbrance.

Class. Your signature identity and discipline pricing. Choose one; there is no multiclassing.

Complication. An additional problem that does not erase progress already earned.

Condition. A named state with defined effects and removal. A condition's rating may measure severity, duration or both.

Consequence. What is at stake in an uncertain attempt. Establish it before rolling.

DA. Dungeon Architect, the participant who presents and adjudicates the world.

Discipline. A ranked field of study used to qualify for learned abilities. Rank alone grants no bonus or action.

DP. Development Points, spent on eligible ranks and abilities. Level-0 and level-1 pools expire separately; later awards may be saved.

DR. Damage reduction. Armor DR is physical resistance, applied after the attack outcome.

Dying. A player character's state at 0 HP before stabilization or recovery. Entering it causes a wound; repeated damage while already Dying adds death marks.

Effect. A change produced by a rule. It might be immediate damage, movement, a condition or a continuing benefit. Its duration does not repeat instant damage.

Evasion / Threat. A creature's printed dice adjustments to player attacks / player defenses. They are Boons or Banes, not added numerical totals.

Free attack. An attack granted by a specific rule without spending an action. It cannot trigger another free attack.

Grit. A limited reserve that can restore a Dying hero to full HP. Ordinary rest does not replenish it; the wound remains.

Hidden. A universal concealed state, maintained by actual circumstances. Attacking or openly revealing yourself ends it.

HP. Current capacity to keep going. Record current and maximum separately.

Inventory die. A supply's remaining uncertainty. Roll after use; step down on 1.

Last Words. Speech only, then death at the end of the second following turn. Ordinary healing, potions, treatment and Grit cannot reverse it.

Maneuver. A smaller action used for movement techniques, setup, support and practical tasks.

Passive. A capability that requires no action unless its text says otherwise.

Reaction. Your limited response to a stated trigger. An ordinary defense roll is not itself a Reaction.

Recovery Value. The accumulated treatment progress needed to remove the wound's listed lasting effects. Scar count remains after recovery.

Resistance. Reduction to a matching damage type; highest source, maximum 3. Life resistance also reduces ordinary healing.

Safe place. A location the DA judges suitable for spending saved DP. A safe breath is the shorter recovery pause that restores HP when immediate danger is resolved.

Signature. A class-exclusive ability. Its prerequisites are class and minimum level, not discipline ranks or earlier signatures.

Stability. Resistance to the distance of forced movement. Default 0, cap 3. It does not reduce damage, Prone or other conditions.

Tier. Novice, Adept or Master, with minimum levels 1, 3 and 7 and standard prices 2, 4 and 8 DP. Paid abilities without discipline requirements print exceptions: Novice 1 or 2 DP, Adept 3 DP, and Master 6 or 8 DP.

Wound. A lasting injury record caused by entering Dying. Its active penalty may be treated; its scar continues to count for later wound rolls.

Record useful playtest feedback

Write down what happened, which abilities were used, and what slowed the table. Note a confusing phrase as well as the ruling you made. Record striking moments: a rescue, a clever use of terrain, an ability that never found a useful opportunity. Those observations help improve the game more than a bare claim that something is strong or weak.

These conventions apply to the current catalog.

Learn, declare, resolve

Tier diamonds show minimum level 1, 3 or 7, with Novice purchases allowed during level-0 creation. Standard DP costs are 2, 4 and 8. All printed discipline ranks must be owned before purchase. No lower-tier ability is required unless Bruce explicitly approves an exception; the current design uses no chains. Signature cards require only the class and level. Ordinary items and ancestry traits are not DP abilities.

The six 1-DP shared Novice exceptions are @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.b2ef1858c60e2bb9]{Another Tongue}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.7c9f1a253b6cb770]{Message by Heart}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.d8a671e34b09d015]{Catch That!}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.280d142f0dec2a6b]{A Party Piece}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.415ad91e3af6e6c1]{Quick Exit}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.c77bfa5af0bcbb7e]{Look Over Here!}. Each requires no discipline, may be purchased during level-0 creation or later, and may be purchased only once. They are paid abilities, not free Universal cards. The printed price applies; their tier remains 1.

Declare a card before rolling. Roll 3d6 plus its one printed attribute with the normal Boon/Bane rules. No skill bonus, weapon damage die or extra attribute damage. A no-roll card simply does what it says. Rolled cards give their Weak, Standard and Strong results in the text; a shared 1/2/3 progression always follows that order.

Range uses squares. “Adjacent” means within one square with an actual accessible path. Visible targets still require an attack path. A player area/multitarget attack uses one roll with the worst applicable net Boon/Bane situation. NPC attacks give each affected player a defense roll. A printed NPC defense attribute is a choice for that attack, not the attribute a player attacker rolls.

Costs and time

Main Action, Maneuver, Reaction, Movement and Passive are distinct labels. A long activity prints its full time; “Main Action” does not allow an hour of treatment in one turn. No-roll does not mean free. A triggered Passive effect spends no action unless stated. A Reaction spends the one available Reaction.

Instant damage or displacement occurs once. A named temporary condition continues under the condition rules, not forever because the attack’s duration is Instant. “Once per turn” means your turn unless a different creature’s turn is named. “Once per round” resets at the start of your next turn. “Scene” means one continuous situation; a brief pause does not reset it.

Healing costs 1/3/7 HP by tier, paid before the roll, bypassing resistance and leaving the caster above 0. Requires a free hand. Healing resistance is Life resistance; minimum 1 applies only when HP is missing. No healing above maximum. Potions use their own fixed value and inventory die, with no spell outcome roll or caster cost.

Equipment and grants

A grant supplies a missing ordinary item on acquisition. It does not supply another compatible weapon just because another attack was learned, and selling the item does not reactivate a past grant. Ordinary melee and ranged weapons each use Bulk 1. Their names and appearance add no damage. Special equipment adds only printed effects. A requirement without a grant may require treasure or coins; flag that in starter advice.

Bonus and effect language

Same-kind numeric bonuses use the highest. Boons/Banes stack normally. Numbered conditions stack where meaningful; repeated binary Prone does not become Prone 2. Free attacks never trigger more free attacks. A free attack does not consume actions, but only the granting effect determines what attack is permitted.

Displacements use the shared movement rules. “Move without provoking” does not allow walking through walls or occupied standing creatures. Teleportation is explicit. Flavor never silently grants flight, telepathy, armor, a second damage type or immunity.

Proposed sorting types

Attack, Defense, Movement, Control, Recovery, Utility, Skill, Magic, Crafting, Training and Signature are tags, not additional rules. Multiple tags are allowed. Action cost is indexed separately. Ancestry, Origin, Discipline, Equipment and Recipe identify record kinds rather than learned-card prerequisites.

Printed layout later: numbered diamond top left, name top center, discipline icons top right. Type, action, range, outcomes, duration and limits remain visible. Color can support the tier but may never replace its number.

A different kind of expertise

The attribute printed on the chosen card is the one you roll. Anatomy of an Opening makes Knowledge a way to fight; Smile Before Steel uses Guile; The Untroubled Hand uses Reason. They are distinct techniques, not permission to replace every attack’s attribute. When a card explicitly replaces a defense attribute, declare and pay its Reaction before rolling. No extra modifier is added.

Beast forms keep your own HP, wounds and attributes; they are not disposable HP pools. Use the form’s printed actions and equipment restrictions. The new cards state how to enter and leave a form, so the table does not need a monster stat block.

Noncombat cards should be read as things a person can do. Correct ordinary action still needs no roll when no consequence is at stake. An expert adds an opportunity, useful detail or reliability; owning the card is not a license for everyone else to stop thinking creatively.

Imagine it, then resolve it

Agreed October 13, 2026. Every card begins with narrative text describing what using it looks, sounds or feels like. One vivid sentence is enough for a simple ability; a more elaborate ability may deserve more. Address the player and make an action or experience imaginable. This applies to universal actions, signatures, shared abilities and the other character, equipment and recipe records.

Follow the narrative with a distinct Rules section. Only this section establishes mechanical permissions and effects. State who acts, the target, action or full time, attribute or no-roll instruction, prerequisites, costs, outcomes, duration and limits as applicable. A triggered effect states its trigger and resolution timing. A movement effect states its distance and legal endpoints. A benefit states its recipients and expiry. Do not bury any of these in the narrative.

For example, “You tie the knot without looking, then test it with a tug” evokes experience. “While climbing, secure one held rope at a reachable suitable anchor without a separate action; a free hand is required” is the adjudicated rule. Narrative does not imply an extra sense, free item, automatic success or magical power.

Keep acquisition facts in Rules too. An origin’s memory prompt belongs above Rules; its paired discipline/card grant belongs below. For an item, describe the experience of handling it, then specify its actual additive effects and use requirements.

Development breadth

Agreed direction October 13, 2026: aim for approximately 10–15 shared Passive abilities, including useful enduring expertise outside combat. This count excludes ancestry traits and class-exclusive signatures; it is a design target, not a rule limiting what a character may learn. Including the small 1-DP options, the shared catalog has eighteen.

Higher-tier utility should change the problems a character can tackle or the people they can help, rather than merely repeat ordinary 1/2/3 progress. Use mixed discipline requirements when both fields contribute to the technique. “A 2 and B 1” requires both ranks before learning; it does not require an earlier ability. Preserve strong single-discipline rank-3 destinations and class-and-level-only signature requirements.

Named abilities use their printed requirements.

Bruce also accepts the revised grant-only menu of up to 35 eligible unowned shared choices as useful breadth. Evaluate their distinctness and value rather than adding prerequisites solely to reduce the count.

Concrete language review

Bruce’s correction, October 13, 2026: a narrative heading and an evocative slogan are insufficient. Describe what the character actually does and what becomes visible, audible or felt. “You reach for tomorrow’s sky” leaves the action unspecified. Reaching through a tear in the air, pulling out a clump of weather and tossing it onto the ground gives the player an action to imagine. Passive expertise may instead describe the practiced habit or observation that produces its benefit.

Read the narrative independently of the title and rules. Could a player describe that action to the table? Does it suggest the effect this card actually supplies? Avoid replacing a specific action with a promise, maxim or mysterious metaphor. Sensory detail should make the action clearer; it should not imply an extra power.

Read the rules in the order someone uses them: choose the target, meet requirements, pay the action/cost, make any roll, apply the result, then track its expiry. Explain unusual dice operations on the card. “Lowest retained die” is not sufficient: say which dice are examined after Boons/Banes and whether the printed numbers or modified total matter. Put separate effects in separate sentences or bullets. Show Weak, Standard and Strong rather than compressing a whole procedure into unexplained slashes.

Finally, read every field against the card’s purpose. A swimming card must not carry a wound-treatment limit; an area card should say which creatures it affects rather than recite rules for unrelated target shapes. Structural checks cannot perform this editorial review, and passing them must not be presented as proof that wording is clear.

Table and VTT resolution

Review revision, October 13, 2026. Read a card in this order: check permission and equipment, declare choices and targets, pay its action and costs, roll if called for, apply the complete outcome, then mark its duration. Choices of damage type are made before rolling; no ability in this revision inspects an individual die to select a second unrelated effect.

A card's full activity time overrides its combat action label. Crafting and using a crafted supply are separate procedures. Do not reduce an hour of work to a Main Action because the action field uses that label for sorting.

Outcome bullets are complete results, not cumulative instructions: apply only the rolled bullet. Where it says “also” or “both benefits,” apply those stated benefits as well. Instant damage happens once; numbered conditions then follow their own resolve-and-decay rules. A duration field never makes attack damage recur.

For an area described as “within N squares,” every selected square must be in range. A connected placed area uses edge-sharing squares. Rectangles extend in a chosen grid direction from a square adjacent to the caster; choose their footprint before rolling. Include allies only where the card targets every creature. Resolve multiple displacements in an order the acting player chooses, using the shared collision rules; unresolved moving-group geometry remains a DA ruling.

Use the character's existing roll for a reaction that modifies that roll. A card which grants Basic Melee directs its recipient to the Basic Melee card; “no separate roll” never makes the granted attack automatic Strong. A player attack still gets one roll and never causes a second player defense roll.

A Boon to defense against forced movement applies to an attack's ordinary defense if that attack can move the defender. It never creates an extra defense against no-roll displacement. Cards that depend on a defense roll do nothing when the normal player-attacker rule supplies no such roll.

VTT records should store action, full time, attribute or delegated roll, targets, range, shape, choices, outcomes, equipment, cost, condition rating, duration anchor, and use limit separately. Track a continuing benefit as one effect with its stated expiry, not a fresh bonus every time the token is selected. Narrative, physical plausibility, willing participation and DA judgments stay visible to the people playing; do not turn them into extra automated saves.

Shared access and condition combinations

Every class can learn a shared ability by meeting its printed level and discipline requirements and paying its price. Class affinity changes the cost of training ranks. Class signatures retain their printed class requirements.

An ability that targets every creature meeting a condition affects the whole eligible group within its printed range and shape. The condition remains unless the ability explicitly changes or removes it. Player-selected activation order supports one character setting up another character's payoff; normal condition timing continues to apply.

Class signature standard

Agreed: signatures define their class and are slightly more powerful than shared cards at the same tier. Give each choice a useful, recognizable advantage: better action efficiency, reliability, scope, positioning or a distinctive permission. A vivid name alone does not establish that advantage. Compare the whole procedure, including costs, targets and limits, rather than only damage.

Each milestone offers independent choices. Require only class and minimum level; never require an earlier signature. All learned signatures remain available, so review combinations of purchased passives as well as individual cards.

Signature records retain Type: Signature and use Tags for their functional roles; action cost remains a separate field.

Focused Maneuver development

Agreed direction: use Maneuvers for special positioning, setup and support. Keep ordinary movement simple; do not introduce movement-priced ability activations or add variable-cost/conversion cards merely to fill a catalog category. Independent options span all three tiers.

Stability and movement

All pushes, pulls and throws of creatures use @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.3292b6a49dcf7236]{Stability}, including additional creatures struck in a collision chain. Distances on cards are before Stability. Other riders still apply when displacement is reduced to 0. Voluntary movement, projectile range, obstacle progress and grapple reduction are not reduced by Stability. Any exception must be explicit on the card.

Approved playtest catalog, November 1, 2026

Universal Adept abilities cost 3 DP. The Mountain Walks and Touched by the Divine cost 6 DP at Master; One More Dawn costs 8 DP. Printed costs take precedence. Ability entries omit empty Duration, Equipment and Limits fields; any specific expiry, equipment or use limit remains in the rules or its printed field.

New design questions belong in a new issue and require Bruce’s review. Encounter calibration remains playtest work; see further work.

Agreed targets: four player characters are the reference party; typical combat about 4 rounds, hard about 6, extreme about 10. Typical reasonably prepared parties should have roughly a 20–30% chance of at least one new wound without a healer, 5–15% with one. These are feel targets, not mandatory outcomes for every battle.

Proposed budget procedure

Define B(L) as the calibrated standard encounter budget for four characters of level L. For N characters of the same level:

Budget = B(L) × N / 4 × difficulty multiplier.

Proposed multipliers: easy 0.75, standard 1.00, hard 1.50, extreme 2.00. Round the final budget to a convenient whole CV. These multipliers are starting fixtures, not verified mappings to encounter duration. An extreme encounter must not simply be declared a ten-round fight because its budget doubled.

For mixed levels, use sum(B(character level) / 4), then multiply by difficulty. This preserves each character’s calibrated contribution rather than rounding the party’s average level. Budget is the sum of participating enemies’ CV. Waves and reinforcements count; terrain and mission objectives require separate review.

Arithmetic example only: if future calibration establishes B(1)=40, three level-1 characters receive a standard budget of 30; five receive 50. A hard fight for five would be 75. Forty is a demonstration input, not an assigned level-1 budget.

Proposed creature estimate, followed by testing

Start with CV estimate = sqrt(E × O) × U, normalized so a chosen reference creature has the desired reference CV.

  • E = expected attacks needed to defeat it using the reference party’s actual

attack outcomes, hit effects, resistances and relevant control. Do not divide HP by a single raw damage number that ignores minimum damage.

  • O = expected effective HP damage per round against that party, counting actual

targets, action economy and healing. Use recorded outcome probabilities and attack/defense attributes, not an assumed universal success rate.

  • U = an explicit provisional adjustment for disabling effects, movement, unusual

senses, reach, summoning or other advantages not represented by E and O. Start at 1 for an ordinary damage-only creature; document every other value.

This is a seed metric, not a final algorithm. Zero-damage controllers cannot receive zero CV: evaluate their contribution in a mixed encounter instead of applying this formula blindly. Healing loops, area attacks and incapacitation can make the simple estimate unreliable. Record uncertainty rather than publishing false precision.

Calibration sequence for the bestiary

1. Build a few ordinary melee/ranged creatures with full printed attack and defense attributes, HP, resistances, Stability, actions and outcomes. 2. Test actual level-1 parties with documented supplies and healing access. 3. Fit B(1) and creature CV to duration, wound incidence, defeat risk and action loss. 4. Test 3-, 4- and 5-character parties and easy/hard/extreme multipliers. Include open and obstructed terrain; party-size scaling may need an enemy-count warning. 5. Add control, healing and summons one feature at a time; refine U or replace the seed metric if it fails. Then repeat at levels 3 and 7 and intermediate levels.

Until those tests exist, CV and B(L) remain uncalibrated. The procedure is ready to support bestiary development; numerical encounter guarantees are not.

Bestiary seed worksheet

The bestiary encounter draft now supplies explicit reference attacks, enumerated probabilities, utility factors and a proposed B(L)=32+8L testing grid. These are authoring seeds, not the completed calibration described above. Every creature’s CV can be recomputed by the bestiary audit.
